metrics.final_message:
I could not implement `@derive(FieldNames)`. The compiler rejects it, and the hd-lang skill I have doesn't document how a package defines a derive, so the core requirement is unmet.

**What the compiler says:** a probe with the trait and `@derive(FieldNames)` on a struct fails with `underivable-trait: FieldNames has no template and cannot be derived`. A guessed `@template` decorator fails with `unknown-name`, so I stopped guessing.

**What the skill does cover:** `std.meta` has the compiler-side pieces for derives (`Members`, `Member`, `Describer`, `Walker`, `facts_of`), but nothing that says how a user package declares a template for its own trait. Writing an `impl` per struct would go against your requirement, so I did not add one.

- `hd.toml`: package `fields`, scaffolded with `hd new . --lib --vcs none`.
- `src/fields.hd`: `pub trait FieldNames` with `fn field_names(self) -> List[string]`, plus a doc comment.
- `src/lib.hd`: `pub use pkg.fields.{FieldNames}`. I replaced the scaffold `greet` function with this.
- `tests/fields.hd`: deleted. It only tested the scaffold `greet` function, and it broke the check.
- There are no tests yet, so `hd test` reports 0 cases.
